key_insight: TRIAGE shows that NVFP4 training instability depends not just on mismatch size, but on whether policy-gradient updates are locally amplifying or contracting, so direction-aware correction can stabilize RL for LLM reasoning.
engineering_relevance: It enables native 4-bit sampler/learner execution with much higher rollout throughput while preserving BF16-level benchmark performance, making low-precision RL more practical for large reasoning models.
method: Diagnose mismatch at the segment level and separate amplifying from contracting update contributions.
Rebalance policy-gradient updates based on direction-aware signals rather than mismatch magnitude alone.
Apply bounded repair only to residual severe mismatch while keeping native W4A4 execution.
evidence_signal: On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, TRIAGE stayed stable through the evaluated training horizon and matched full-precision performance on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, with up to 2.3x higher rollout throughput than BF16.
watch_item: The approach depends on segment-level mismatch diagnosis and bounded repair rules, so implementation complexity and sensitivity to diagnosis quality may be important in new RL pipelines.
paper_title: TRIAGE: Direction-Aware Mismatch Stabilization of Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
